claims.text: ⍉red flags or CA risk: new localized or gen nodes can be observed for up to 4 wks.
claims.quote: Patients with newly identified localized or generalized adenopathy and no systemic symptoms, red flags, increased risk or suspicion of malignancy can safely be observed for up to 4 weeks, unless cancer is suspected

claims.text: Red flags or gen nodes: CBC and CXR; abnorm white cells lead to smear and flow cytometry.
claims.quote: Patients with unexplained red flag findings and those with generalized adenopathy should have a complete blood count (CBC) and chest radiograph (1). If abnormal white blood cells are seen on CBC, a peripheral smear and flow cytometry are performed to evaluate for leukemia or lymphoma.

claims.text: US first for localized nodes; CT or MRI if CA = sus or nodes persist unexplained in those > 14.
claims.quote: Imaging of localized lymphadenopathy often begins with ultrasound, especially in children ≤ 14 years of age

claims.text: Bx if malig = sus or nodes do ⍉resolve in 3 to 4 wks; core needle bx = a good first choice.
claims.quote: Biopsy is also considered if isolated or generalized adenopathy does not resolve in 3 to 4 weeks (3), or if a cause is not apparent despite a thorough diagnostic evaluation. Tissue can be obtained by fine needle aspirate, core needle biopsy, or excisional biopsy; core needle biopsy is a good initial choice
